explanation.en:
The て-form is a special verb form used to connect actions, make requests, and build many grammar patterns. It is one of the most important forms in beginner Japanese.

Key points:
• The て-form connects actions: 行って、食べます
• It is used in requests: 〜てください
• It appears in many patterns like 〜ている, 〜てもいい
• The verb ending changes based on the verb group

For う-verbs, the ending changes (e.g., 書く → 書いて, 読む → 読んで, 話す → 話して). For る-verbs, drop る and add て (食べる → 食べて). The irregular verbs are する → して and 来る → 来て.

At N5, you do not need to memorize every rule at once. Start with common verbs and practice their て-forms. This form will show up repeatedly, so recognizing it is more important than producing it perfectly at first.

A simple use is connecting two actions: “朝ご飯を食べて学校に行きます” means “I eat breakfast and go to school.” The て-form makes the first action feel like a step before the next.

Once you know the て-form, you can use many other patterns, so it is worth practicing carefully.

examples.japanese: 朝ご飯を食べて学校に行きます。
examples.romaji: Asagohan o tabete gakkou ni ikimasu.
examples.english: I eat breakfast and go to school.
I read a book and sleep.

examples.japanese: テレビを見て休みます。
友だちに会って話します。
examples.english: I meet a friend and talk.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using dictionary form to connect actions
commonMistakes.correction: Use the て-form for the first action
commonMistakes.example: ❌ 食べる行きます → ✅ 食べて行きます

commonMistakes.correction: する→して, 来る→来て
